arxiv-2103-06281.title: Renormalization of the C2HDM with FeynMaster 2
arxiv-2103-06281.creator: Duarte Fontes, Jorge C. Romão
arxiv-2103-06281.description: Abstract We present the one-loop electroweak renormalization of the CP-violating 2-Higgs-Doublet Model with softly broken ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} symmetry (C2HDM). The existence of CP violation in the scalar sector of the model leads to a quite unique process of renormalization, since it requires the introduction of several non-physical parameters.

arxiv-2104-11905.title: Superharmonic double-well systems with zero-energy ground states: Relevance for diffusive relaxation scenarios
arxiv-2104-11905.creator: Piotr Garbaczewski and Vladimir A. Stephanovich
arxiv-2104-11905.description: Abstract Relaxation properties (specifically time-rates) of the Smoluchowski diffusion process on a line, in a confining potential U ⁡ ( x ) ∼ x m U(x)\sim x^{m} , m = 2 ​ n ≥ 2 m=2n\geq 2 , can be spectrally quantified by means of the affiliated Schrödinger semigroup exp ⁡ ( − t ​ H ^ ) \exp(-t\hat{H}) ,

arxiv-2205-00369.title: Optimizing an Adaptive Fuzzy Logic Controller of a 3-DOF Helicopter with a Modified PSO Algorithm
arxiv-2205-00369.creator: Shokoufeh Naderi Département Génie Électrique & Génie Informatique Université de Sherbrooke shokoufeh.naderi@usherbrooke.ca, Maude J. Blondin Département Génie Électrique & Génie Informatique Université de Sherbrooke maude.blondin2@usherbrooke.ca, Behrooz Rezaie Faculty of Electrical and Computer En
arxiv-2205-00369.description: Abstract This paper investigates the controller optimization for a helicopter system with three degrees of freedom (3-DOF). To control the system, we combined fuzzy logic with adaptive control theory. The system is extensively nonlinear and highly sensitive to the controller’s parameters, making it a real challenge to study these parameters’ effect on the controller’s performance.

arxiv-2205-09876.title: Hunting for vampires and other unlikely forms of parity violation at the Large Hadron Collider
arxiv-2205-09876.creator: Christopher G. Lester ∗, Radha Mastandrea ∗, Daniel Noel ∗, Rupert Tombs
arxiv-2205-09876.description: Abstract Abstract Non-Standard-Model parity violation may be occurring in LHC collisions. Any such violation would go unseen, however, as searches are for it are not currently performed. One barrier to searches for parity violation is the lack of model-independent methods sensitive to all of its forms.

arxiv-2211-08256.title: The q-Binomial Coefficient for Negative Arguments and Some q-Binomial Summation Identities
arxiv-2211-08256.creator: M.J. Kronenburg
arxiv-2211-08256.description: Abstract Using a property of the q-shifted factorial, an identity for q-binomial coefficients is proved, which is used to derive the formulas for the q-binomial coefficient for negative arguments. The result is in agreement with an earlier paper about the normal binomial coefficient for negative arguments.

arxiv-2310-18842.title: Optimization of Nonlinear Turbulence in Stellarators
arxiv-2310-18842.creator: P. Kim \aff 1,3 \corresp, S. Buller \aff 2 R. Conlin \aff 1, W. Dorland \aff 2, 3, D. W. Dudt \aff 1, R. Gaur \aff 1, R. Jorge \aff 4,5. E. Kolemen \aff 1,6, M. Landreman \aff 2, N. R. Mandell \aff 6, D. Panici \aff 1
arxiv-2310-18842.description: Abstract We present new stellarator equilibria that have been optimized for reduced turbulent transport using nonlinear gyrokinetic simulations within the optimization loop. The optimization routine involves coupling the pseudo-spectral GPU-native gyrokinetic code GX with the stellarator equilibrium and optimization code DESC . Since using GX allows for fast nonlinear simulations, we directly optimize for reduced nonlinear heat fluxes.

arxiv-2402-10181.title: Extracting randomness from quantum ‘magic’
arxiv-2402-10181.creator: Christopher Vairogs, Bin Yan
arxiv-2402-10181.description: Abstract Magic is a critical property of quantum states that plays a pivotal role in fault-tolerant quantum computation. Simultaneously, random states have emerged as a key element in various randomized techniques within contemporary quantum science. In this study, we establish a direct connection between these two notions.

arxiv-2510-12028.title: Perceived Fairness in Networks
arxiv-2510-12028.creator: Arthur Charpentier
arxiv-2510-12028.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Arthur Charpentier. The usual definitions of algorithmic fairness focus on population-level statistics, such as demographic parity or equal opportunity. However, in many social or economic contexts, fairness is not perceived globally, but locally, through an individual’s peer network and comparisons. We propose a theoretical model of perceived fairness networks, in which each individual’s sense of discrimination depends on the local topology of interactions.

arxiv-2512-14370.title: From bipedal to chaotic motion of chemically fueled partially wetting liquid drops
arxiv-2512-14370.creator: Florian Voss, Uwe Thiele
arxiv-2512-14370.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Florian Voss, Uwe Thiele. We employ a thermodynamically consistent out-of-equilibrium continuum model to study the motion patterns of partially wetting liquid drops covered by autocatalytically reacting surfactants. When ambient chemostats feed a chemomechanical feedback loop involving a nonlinear reaction network, surface stresses caused by the Marangoni effect and the ensuing hydrodynamic motion, drops show a variety of increasingly complex biomimetic motility modes including shuttling, bipedal, rotational, intermittently chaotic and chaotic motion.

arxiv-2602-08667.title: SRSUPM: Sequential Recommender System Based on User Psychological Motivation
arxiv-2602-08667.creator: Yicheng Di, Yuan Liu, Zhi Chen, Jingcai Guo
arxiv-2602-08667.description: Abstract Sequential recommender infers users’ evolving psychological motivations from historical interactions to recommend the next preferred items. Most existing methods compress recent behaviors into a single vector and optimize it toward a single observed target item, but lack explicit modeling of psychological motivation shift.

pmc-10622391.title: Bernese periacetabular osteotomy (PAO): from its local inception to its worldwide adoption
pmc-10622391.creator: Reinhold Ganz, Michael Leunig
pmc-10622391.description: The development of the Bernese periacetabular osteotomy (PAO) is based on a structured approach starting with an analysis of the preexisting procedures to improve the coverage of the femoral head and was followed by a list of additional goals and improvements.

pmc-10636167.title: Dual-radionuclide in vivo imaging of micro-metastasis and lymph tract with submillimetre resolution
pmc-10636167.creator: Atsushi Yagishita, Shin’ichiro Takeda, Kazunobu Ohnuki, Miho Katsuragawa, Oltea Sampetrean, Hirofumi Fujii, Tadayuki Takahashi
pmc-10636167.description: Multi-radionuclide in vivo imaging with submillimetre resolution can be a potent tool for biomedical research. While high-resolution radionuclide imaging faces challenges in sensitivity, multi-radionuclide imaging encounters difficulty due to radiation contamination, stemming from crosstalk between radionuclides and Compton scattering. Addressing these challenges simultaneously is imperative for multi-radionuclide high-resolution imaging.

pmc-11566669.title: An updated review for clinical and radiological predictors of acute intraparenchymal hematoma progression in cerebral contusion
pmc-11566669.creator: Gengyu Chen, Huibin Kang
pmc-11566669.description: BackgroundsThe rapid expansion of an intraparenchymal hematoma following cerebral contusion often results in high mortality rates and a poor prognosis. Effective tools are essential for predicting and monitoring the incidence of traumatic intraparenchymal hematoma (tICH) and identifying patients at high risk of tICH expansion. This enables timely surgical interventions and appropriate medical management.

pmc-11652784.title: Exploring the Synergistic Effects of Erinacines on Microglial Regulation and Alzheimer's Pathology Under Metabolic Stress
pmc-11652784.creator: Van Thanh Bui, Kuan‐Wei Wu, Chin‐Chu Chen, Anh Thuc Nguyen, Wei‐Jan Huang, Li‐Ya Lee, Wan‐Ping Chen, Chi‐Ying Huang, Young‐Ji Shiao
pmc-11652784.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background Hericium erinaceus mycelium and its constituents, erinacines A and S, have shown neuroprotective effects in APP/PS1 transgenic mice; however, the precise mechanisms by which they modulate microglial phenotypes remain unclear. Our study is the first to explore the effect of erinacines on microglia morphology and the underlying mechanisms using a novel primary mixed glia cell model and advanced bioinformatic tools.

pmc-12418710.title: Older adults’ perspectives on physical activity during hospitalization: a qualitative interview study
pmc-12418710.creator: Kristina Dalin Eriksson, Anna-Karin Welmer, Linda Sandberg, Anne-Marie Boström
pmc-12418710.description: BackgroundThe benefits of physical activity for frail older acutely hospitalized adults are becoming increasingly clear. To enhance opportunities for physical activity on geriatric wards, it is essential to understand the older adult’s perspective.AimThe aim of the study was to explore the experiences and perceptions of physical activity among older adults during hospital stays on a geriatric ward.

pmc-12714540.title: Infusion-Related Reactions Among Cancer Patients Receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: The ARON-MOUSEION-013 Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-12714540.creator: Elsa Vitale, Alessandro Rizzo, Lorenza Maistrello, Omar Cauli, Oronzo Brunetti, Fernando Sabino Marques Monteiro, Andrey Soares, Matteo Santoni, Veronica Mollica, Francesco Massari
pmc-12714540.description: PurposeTo investigate the incidence of Infusion-Related Reactions (IRRs) among cancer patients receiving Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors (ICIs) and immune-based combinations.Patients and MethodsThe ARON-MOUSEION-013 was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251018433). Observational, randomized and quasi-experimental studies were included in the present review, and rates in IRR among cancer adults (≥18 years) receiving ICIs were recorded and then analyzed.

pmc-12742154.title: Investigating the potential of Anystis baccarum (Acari: Anystidae) and Orius insidiosus (Heteroptera: Anthocoridae) as biological control agents for Thrips parvispinus (Thysanoptera: Thripidae) in laboratory and greenhouse cage trials

pmc-12742154.description: Thrips parvispinus (Karny) is a tropical thrips species that recently spread across the world. Extensive plant damage caused by T. parvispinus results in serious losses for growers, for this species feeds mostly on young leaves and flowers. Among many host plants, peppers are readily attacked by T. parvispinus across its geographical range. Effective and sustainable control methods for T.

pmc-12978214.title: A previously unrecognized class of fungal ice-nucleating proteins with bacterial ancestry
pmc-12978214.creator: Rosemary J. Eufemio, Mariah Rojas, Kaden Shaw, Ingrid de Almeida Ribeiro, Hao-Bo Guo, Galit Renzer, Kassaye Belay, Haijie Liu, Parkesh Suseendran, Xiaofeng Wang, Janine Fröhlich-Nowoisky, Ulrich Pöschl, Mischa Bonn, Rajiv J. Berry, Valeria Molinero, Boris A. Vinatzer, Konrad Meister
pmc-12978214.description: Ice-nucleating proteins (INpros) catalyze ice formation at high subzero temperatures, with major biological and environmental implications. While bacterial INpros have been structurally characterized, their counterparts in other organisms have remained largely unknown. Here, we identify membrane-independent proteins in fungi of the Mortierellaceae family that promote ice formation with high efficiency.

pmc-13295329.title: Endogenous Sulfane Sulfur Mediates the Oxidative Stress Response Process in Pseudomonas aeruginosa
pmc-13295329.creator: Weining Sun, Xiaoqian Guo, Feng Chen, Guangyu Liu
pmc-13295329.description: Sulfane sulfur species are increasingly recognized as integral cellular components involved in signaling pathways and cytoprotection against oxidative stress in mammals. While their production in bacteria has been extensively studied, their functional role in bacterial oxidative stress defense remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that sulfane sulfur generated by sulfide: quinone oxidoreductase decreases H2O2 sensitivity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1.

pmc-13335694.title: Atroposelective Construction of Axially Chiral Tetraarylethenes Via NHC‐Catalyzed Desymmetrization
pmc-13335694.creator: Yang‐Ze Zheng, Ting‐Rui Luan, Ming‐Hao Song, Zhaofeng Sun, Chuan‐Jun Lu, Long‐Long Xi, Ren‐Rong Liu
pmc-13335694.description: We report the first NHC‐catalyzed atroposelective synthesis of axially chiral tetraarylethenes (TAEs) via oxidative desymmetrization of prochiral TAE dialdehydes. This catalytic strategy operates under mild conditions and accommodates a broad range of phenolic and nitrogen nucleophiles, delivering diverse axially chiral TAEs in good yields and up to 99% ee.

pmc-13354808.title: Diagnostic value of routine endoscopic studies in staging locally advanced cervical cancer: a multicenter experience from a low and middle-income country
pmc-13354808.creator: Jorge Hoegl, Andreina Fernandes, Fernando Hidalgo, Sunangela Escalona, Anthony López, Yetsy Muñoz, Paola Morillo, Mary Carmen Hidalgo, Luisa López, María Briceño, María Mercedes Pérez
pmc-13354808.description: Objective:To evaluate the diagnostic value of routine cystoscopy and rectosigmoidoscopy in staging locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC) in a low - middle - income country (LMIC) setting.Material and methods:A multicenter, retrospective cohort study of 233 patients with LACC (International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics 2018 stages IB3–IVB) in Venezuela.

pmc-13540821.title: Telmisartan-based monotherapy and combination regimens for blood pressure control in adults with hypertension: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and GRADE assessment
pmc-13540821.creator: Baraah Abu Alsel, Muzun Saleh Alturqi Alanazi, Aryam Salem Mgairan Alrawaili, Shahad Ayed Alenezi, Safya E Esmaeel, Manal S Fawzy, Yehia Nabil
pmc-13540821.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeTo evaluate the efficacy, safety, and certainty of evidence for telmisartan-based antihypertensive regimens in adults with hypertension.MethodsThis systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception to 2026. Eligible studies enrolled adults with hypertension and compared telmisartan monotherapy or telmisartan-containing combinations with placebo, usual care, non-telmisartan antihypertensive agents, or alternative telmisartan-based regimens.
